newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 17.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 17.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HANOVER - Private TV broadcaster RTL is fined more than 19 million marks ($11 million) of advertising revenues after a federal state court ruled that it showed too many commercials during its films. The channel was found to have breached advertising regulations on more than 30 occasions between 1993 and 1994.
(Reuter)

MAINZ - TV commercials reach 86 percent of the viewers of the programme during which they are shown, according to a study by the Sat. 1 commercial channel. Only one in nine viewers who took part on the 1996 survey switched channels or turned the television off during commercial breaks. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Frankfurt-based Lowe Koch Media names Konrad Geipel and Sean Pattison as its new business managers. Geipel comes from DMB&B-subsidiary Mediacenter while Pattison was working for McCann-Erickson in Budapest. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Jeans manufacturer Mustang says it is to work more closely with New York agency RSY after its contract with Leonhardt & Kern expires on June 30. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German media giant Bertelsmann AG and Bavarian rival Leo Kirch are in intensive negotiations that could lead to close cooperation of their joint pay TV channel Premiere and Kirch's upstart DF1, the companies confirm. Officials from both companies however rule out a magazine report suggesting the cooperation could go as far as a merger of Premiere and DF1.
(Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Political affairs television programmes are more frequently using violent scenes as content designed to attract viewers, according to a long-term study by the regional broadcasting authority of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. The quality of their overall content was not, however, deteriorating nor showing increased political bias, the research found. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Internet service-provider AOL says it has some 350,000 customers in Germany, with 600,000 across Europe.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LEVERKUSEN - Chemicals group Bayer founds its 10th joint venture in China to develop polyurethanes with a unit of China's National Petrochemical Corp. Bayer will own 55 percent of the joint venture Jinling Petrochemical Corp (JCP). (Reuter)

AACHEN - Insurer Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs AG (AMB) says it expects group profits in 1997 to be at least as high as in 1996, when net earnings rose some 31 percent to 343.4 million marks. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Carmaker Adam Opel says it is developing a new small car to compete against rivals Volkswagen and Ford in the highly competitive market segment. Opel managing director David Herman tells Reuters the new car would compete against the Seat Arosa, which was unveiled last March at the Geneva car show, and against the two-door Ford Ka. (Reuter)

PULLACH - Car rental group Sixt says sales and earnings were up in the first five months of the year and predicts that car rental sales would be at least 900 million marks in 1997. Car rental turnover of 753 million marks in 1996. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Armin Reins, who quit DMB&B as Executive Creative Director only a year ago to join a unit of Wilkens, is to leave his new firm at the end of the month. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Hans Schmahl, deputy chief editor of the Hamburg-based Die Welt newspaper is to replace Wilhelm Furler in the same position at the Berliner Morgenpost daily. (Kress)
WWALLDORF - Michel Friedmann, a lawyer and a member of the presidium of the Central Jewish Council in Germany is from September to host a weekly chat show on the pay-TV channel Premiere (Kress).
